claims.text: The target material is a CoCrFeMnNi-based high-entropy alloy with tailored Al additions.
The alloy is homogeneous and has a uniform as-cast microstructure.
High configurational entropy reduces atomic mobility and produces sluggish diffusion in the Al-modified CoCrFeMnNi alloy.
Sluggish diffusion restricts the outward migration of metal ions, especially Al and Cr.
Sluggish diffusion restricts inward oxygen transport.
The oxide scale formed on the HEA consists primarily of Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
Constrained diffusion promotes a continuous, thin, uniform, and adherent oxide scale.
Restricted ionic and oxygen transport prevents excessive scale thickening and spallation.
A continuous protective Al2O3/Cr2O3-containing scale retards further oxidation.
The HEA will develop a thinner oxide scale than a conventional Ni-Cr-Al alloy under identical oxidation conditions.
The HEA scale will adhere better and undergo less spallation than the scale on the conventional Ni-Cr-Al alloy.
The HEA will exhibit greater oxidation resistance than the conventional Ni-Cr-Al baseline.
Bulk diffusivities of key species in the HEA will be significantly lower than in the conventional Ni-Cr-Al alloy.
The conventional Ni-Cr-Al baseline has faster diffusion rates than the HEA.
Faster diffusion in the conventional Ni-Cr-Al alloy produces thicker, less uniform, and more spallation-prone scales.
The proposed hypothesis is bounded to synthetic-air oxidation at 900-1000 °C for approximately 50-200 hours.
Alloy composition, grain-boundary density, minor alloying elements, and processing defects may alter the proposed behavior.
The controlled comparison uses identical isothermal oxidation conditions for the HEA and a conventional Ni-Cr-Al alloy.
Tracer measurements will distinguish bulk diffusion from grain-boundary diffusion for key species such as Al and Cr.
The hypothesis is falsified if the HEA lacks lower bulk diffusivity or does not consistently produce a thinner and more adherent scale than the baseline.
